newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's PUMA Euro issue oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's PUMA Euro issue oversubscribed.

text.p: Macquarie Bank's securitisation arm, PUMA Management Ltd, made its first foray into Euro market on Monday, and its US$700 million issue was heavily oversubscribed.
"Despite the fact that we are a relative newcomer, PUMA has achieved pricing which is better than many European mortgage-back bond issues," said PUMA's Managing Director Tony Gill.
"This reflects the quality of the Australian mortgage portfolio and PUMA's ability to deliver highly rated securitites to European investors," Gill said in London after the launch of the issue.
The issue, known as E-1 Series 1, was split into three tranches and was priced at a weighted average margin over time of 11.3 basis points over LIBOR.
Gill said the structure of the deal, rated AAA/Aaa, allowed for an extremely competitive pricing which compares favourably with its domestic pricing.

"This is the first time an Australian issuer has issued foreign currency debt offshore with a credit rating which out-ranks the sovereign rating. This is also the largest ever Euro-issue by an Australian private sector entity," Gill added.

Gill said the ability to access the offshore market was a major step forward in diversifying its funding pool and provides further assurance that its strategic partner, Aussie Home Loans, will continue to provide competitively priced home loans in Australia.
This Euro-issue, which is part of a A$3.0 billion funding programme for calender 1997, was lead managed by J.P. Morgan with Deutsche Morgan Grenfell as co-lead and UBS and SBC Warburg as co-managers.
